Introduction
The CO2 automatic fire extinguishing system consists of a number of cylinders containing carbon dioxide gas in its liquid state at a pressure of approximately 80 bar. These cylinders are arranged in groups according to the quantity of gas required for extinguishing, and each group is dedicated to extinguishing a fire in a specific area commensurate with the volume of gas inside these cylinders. There are extinguishing gas sprinklers and flame detectors distributed as in the following table:-
Flame detector | Heat detector | Sprinklers | Number of cylinders | 
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Right combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 4 | 3 | Left combustion chamber
1 | 4 | 8 | 7 | Oil tank
Each of the flame and heat detectors has two independent lines, and for the fire system to operate, a fire alarm signal must come from one of the fire detectors on the first line together with an alarm from one of the fire detectors on the second line; then the weight-release solenoid moves and the fire system operates. At the same time, the emergency trip signal goes from the limit switch to the various components of the unit so that they stop.
The cylinder weighing device is the indicator of a leak of the extinguishing agent from the carbon dioxide cylinder, and the leak indicator device is adjusted so that it gives a signal of a leak when the cylinder loses at most 10% of its total weight, where cylindrical weight No. 1 drops down when this happens, and this is the indicator of a drop in the cylinder weight as a result of a gas leak, so it is replaced.
This document was prepared by Eng. Yousry Abdel Halim Abdel Latif and tested by Eng. Wasfy William Nashed - Senior Engineer, Occupational Safety and Health Department - and approved by Eng. Mohamed Hussein Gomaa, Head of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control Sector at the East Delta Electricity Production Company.

Release the cylindrical weight to undo tightening nuts No. 3 | 1.
Turn cylindrical weight No. 1 counter-clockwise on threaded shaft No. 2 until the cylindrical weight is barely balanced horizontally | 2.
Tighten the cylindrical weight clockwise by three turns | 3
Tighten tightening nuts No. 3 and secure the position of the cylindrical weight with fixing wire No. 4 | 4
